Jollity

JOL-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Jollity is lively, cheerful merriment or festivity.

Even the strictest teacher couldn't resist a smile at the sheer jollity of the third-graders' costume parade.

Worked Example

The reunion hall echoed with jollity late into the night, as three generations of cousins traded stories and danced to the same old records.

Jollity is more than just happiness -- it's an outward, shared, boisterous kind of merriment.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

merriment: Merriment is cheerful fun and laughter at any scale -- one shared joke can make a moment of merriment. Jollity is merriment turned all the way up: the loud, outward, boisterous cheer of a whole room celebrating together, never a small private smile.

gaiety: Gaiety is lighthearted, cheerful high spirits -- the bright, bubbly mood of a person or a gathering. Jollity is heartier and noisier: not just the mood but the merrymaking itself, a room loud with laughter, songs, and celebration.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

gloom: a feeling of sadness or despair

solemnity: a serious, formal, dignified manner

Where it sits · how loud and lively the fun gets — amusement → jollity → revelry

amusement vs. jollity: Amusement is a mild, quiet sense of being entertained, far calmer than the shared merriment of jollity.

revelry vs. jollity: Revelry is even more unrestrained and wild than ordinary jollity, often involving loud parties late into the night.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — jolly

root — jolly: full of high spirits; cheerful (Old French jolif, 'pleasant, festive')

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Jollity is simply jolly ('full of high spirits') plus -ity ('the state of') -- literally 'the state of being jolly.'
